attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given as his view, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense observation. The original suggests the scenario is the most underrepresented one; the normalisation keeps the core claim that it is underrepresented. That is acceptable and does not overstate.

contract.note: The plain reading (prominent US/UK policy discussion in early 2025 gives too little serious weight to AGI not being near) is ordinary and fair. It requires a comparative benchmark the speaker did not supply, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: A genuine Jan 2025 policy-facing report that says slow progress is possible. It is one document and a brief hedge. It does not measure relative attention across policy discussion, and the contract says isolated counterexamples do not settle the claim.
A genuine Jan 2025 UK plan that briefly considers slower progress but says experts on balance expect rapid progress. It is a single document and does not measure overall representation.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs a representative comparison of how much policy discussion treats AGI as imminent versus not. The packet has only two individual documents that acknowledge slower progress in passing, and it says itself that no comparative analysis or benchmark was found. Isolated counterexamples cannot settle the claim either way, so the outcome is unresolved.
